# Morning memo — 2026-09-18

**Source failures (if any):** none surfaced in the fetch log. 40 items claimed; pre-triage removed 1 duplicate and deferred 24 over the per-source cap, leaving 15 scored.

## Worth attention

- **TypeSafe AI's Jev now available on AI Gateway** — https://vercel.com/changelog/typesafe-ai-jev-now-available-on-ai-gateway
  Vercel's AI Gateway now serves Jev, a probabilistic decision model that returns typed Choice / Score / Boolean answers with probabilities instead of generating text you then parse. TypeSafe claims up to 193.6x faster and 444.6x cheaper than LLMs on its own workflow evals, exposed through AI SDK 7's experimental `evaluate` API (7.0.105+). If it holds up, the classification and scoring steps in nightly-librarian and similar pipelines are exactly the shape this targets — worth a small bake-off against the current model call before trusting the vendor numbers.

- **Keys Not Included: recovering the signing keys for US driver's license barcodes** — https://ryan.science/blog/keys-not-included
  Independent research into recovering the signing keys behind the PDF417 barcodes on US driver's licenses. If the signing keys are recoverable, a cryptographically "valid" barcode stops being proof that a license is genuine. Direct relevance to any identity or contractor-verification flow that treats a barcode scan as a trust anchor — Veremun/ContractorVerify included. Treat barcode signature checks as one weak signal, not verification.

- **Forgery of C2PA on a Pixel 10** — https://www.hackerfactor.com/blog/index.php?/archives/1102-C2PA-and-Pixel-Glitter-Milk.html
  Hackerfactor demonstrates forging C2PA content credentials on a Pixel 10, undercutting the assumption that hardware-attested provenance metadata proves an image is real. Anyone planning to lean on C2PA for document or photo authenticity in a verification product should not treat the credential as dispositive.

- **Mem0 joins the Vercel Marketplace** — https://vercel.com/changelog/mem0-joins-the-vercel-marketplace
  Mem0 is now a native Vercel Marketplace integration: scoped project and API key provisioned automatically as env vars, billed on the Vercel invoice, no separate account. Removes the key-management and second-vendor friction for adding long-term memory to an agent. Narrow in that the convenience only exists if you are already deploying on Vercel.

- **Nvidia announces native GPU programming in Rust** — https://developer.nvidia.com/blog/introducing-cuda-rust-two-tracks-for-writing-gpu-kernels/
  Nvidia is shipping two supported tracks for writing CUDA kernels in Rust. A real ecosystem shift for anyone doing GPU work in Rust; no near-term action for a web/agent shop, but it changes the medium-term calculus for systems-level ML tooling.

- **My temporary PHP fix from 2014 has nearly 20M installs. Today I'm deprecating it** — https://jakeasmith.com/blog/http-build-url/
  Maintainer is deprecating a stopgap PHP package with ~20M installs. Actionable only for PHP shops, but a clean reminder that transitive "temporary" dependencies outlive the problem they patched.

- **Training a 4B model to produce 81% faster query plans than Postgres** — https://rohanbansal.com/qorl
  Claims an RL-trained 4B model beats the Postgres planner by 81% on query plan quality. Single-source, no independent reproduction seen — tracking rather than acting. Fits the broader pattern worth watching: small task-specific models displacing both hand-tuned heuristics and general LLMs.

- **Xiaomi Mimo 2.6 live post-training dashboard** — https://mimo.xiaomi.com/rl/
  Xiaomi is publishing a live dashboard of an RL post-training run. Unusual transparency into open-model training; nothing to act on, but a useful signal on the pace of non-US open model work.

results.title: TypeSafe AI's Jev now available on AI Gateway
results.summary: Vercel's AI Gateway now serves Jev, a probabilistic decision model that returns typed Choice, Score, and Boolean answers with probabilities rather than generating text an app must parse and validate. TypeSafe reports up to 193.6x faster and 444.6x cheaper than LLMs on its own workflow evaluations, exposed through AI SDK 7's experimental evaluate API (7.0.105+). For pipelines whose LLM calls are really classification or scoring, this is a plausible cost and latency lever. Benchmark it against your current model call before trusting the vendor multiples.
results.raw_claim: Jev, a typed probabilistic decision model from TypeSafe AI, is now available on Vercel AI Gateway via the AI SDK 7 experimental evaluate API, with vendor-reported gains up to 193.6x faster and 444.6x cheaper than LLMs.
results.uncertainty: The speed and cost multiples come from TypeSafe's own workflow evaluations with no independent reproduction, and the evaluate API is still experimental.
results.worth_mentioning_reason: Directly targets the classification and scoring calls that dominate agent pipeline cost, including nightly-librarian's own triage step.
results.verdict_reason: Concrete platform availability plus a real cost/latency decision for anyone running classification-shaped LLM calls.

results.title: Keys Not Included: recovering the signing keys for US driver's license barcodes
results.summary: Independent research into recovering the cryptographic signing keys behind the PDF417 barcodes printed on US driver's licenses. If those keys are recoverable, a barcode that verifies as correctly signed is no longer evidence that the license itself is genuine. Any identity or contractor-verification flow that treats a barcode scan as a trust anchor should downgrade it to one weak signal among several.
results.raw_claim: Signing keys used for US driver's license PDF417 barcodes can be recovered, undermining barcode signature verification as proof of document authenticity.
results.uncertainty: Full content was not retrieved by the fetcher, so the exact scope — which jurisdictions and how practical the recovery is — is unconfirmed from the title and source alone.
results.worth_mentioning_reason: Bears directly on identity-verification product design, including Veremun/ContractorVerify.
results.verdict_reason: Credible security research that invalidates a common assumption in ID-verification flows.

results.title: Forgery of C2PA on a Pixel 10
results.summary: Hackerfactor demonstrates forging C2PA content credentials on a Pixel 10, undercutting the claim that hardware-backed provenance metadata proves an image is authentic. The practical takeaway is that a valid C2PA manifest establishes a chain of assertions, not truth. Products planning to rely on content credentials for document or photo authenticity need a second, independent signal.
results.raw_claim: C2PA content credentials can be forged on a Pixel 10, so a valid C2PA manifest does not prove an image is authentic.
results.uncertainty: Only the title and source were retrieved; the precise forgery technique and whether it requires device access is not confirmed here.
results.worth_mentioning_reason: Changes how much weight a verification product should place on content provenance metadata.
results.verdict_reason: Credible researcher undermining a provenance standard that many verification roadmaps assume is sound.

results.title: Mem0 joins the Vercel Marketplace
results.summary: Mem0, a long-term memory layer for AI agents, is now a native Vercel Marketplace integration. Installing it provisions a scoped project and API key automatically as project environment variables and bills through the Vercel invoice, with no separate account or key management. Vercel also published an eve Memory Agent template showing it end to end. Useful if you are already on Vercel and adding persistent memory to an agent; no benefit otherwise.
results.raw_claim: Mem0 is now a native Vercel Marketplace integration with auto-provisioned API keys and consolidated Vercel billing.
results.uncertainty: Pricing relative to running Mem0 directly is not stated in the changelog.
results.worth_mentioning_reason: Removes onboarding friction for agent memory, a recurring need in MCP and agent work.
results.verdict_reason: Real convenience win but scoped to teams already deploying on Vercel.

results.title: Nvidia announces native GPU programming in Rust
results.summary: Nvidia introduced CUDA-Rust, offering two supported tracks for writing GPU kernels in Rust. That makes Rust a first-class option for GPU work rather than a community-maintained binding. No immediate action for a web or agent shop, but it shifts the medium-term picture for systems-level ML and numerical tooling.
results.raw_claim: Nvidia announced native support for writing CUDA GPU kernels in Rust via two supported tracks.
results.uncertainty: Content body was not retrieved; maturity and feature parity of each track versus C++ CUDA is unconfirmed.
results.worth_mentioning_reason: First-party vendor support meaningfully changes the viability of Rust for GPU work.
results.verdict_reason: Credible first-party ecosystem shift, but narrow scope for a one-person application shop.

results.title: My temporary PHP fix from 2014 has nearly 20M installs. Today I'm deprecating it
results.summary: The maintainer of a stopgap PHP package written in 2014 is deprecating it after roughly 20 million installs. Actionable only if you have PHP in the stack, but it is a clean case study in how long a temporary dependency survives and how much of an ecosystem ends up resting on one unpaid maintainer.
results.raw_claim: The maintainer of the PHP http_build_url polyfill is deprecating it after nearly 20 million installs.
results.uncertainty: Deprecation timeline and whether a maintained successor exists were not retrieved.
results.worth_mentioning_reason: Concrete dependency-risk example with a named deprecation, not just commentary.
results.verdict_reason: Real and specific, but only actionable for PHP users.

results.title: Training a 4B model to produce 81% faster query plans than Postgres
results.summary: A write-up claiming a 4B-parameter model trained with reinforcement learning produces query plans 81% faster than the Postgres planner. If it reproduces, it is another data point that small task-specific models can beat both hand-tuned heuristics and general LLMs. Single source with no independent reproduction visible, so this is worth tracking rather than acting on.
results.raw_claim: A 4B-parameter RL-trained model reportedly produces query plans 81% faster than the Postgres query planner.
results.uncertainty: Single-author blog post; benchmark methodology, workload mix, and reproducibility are unverified.
results.worth_mentioning_reason: Fits a pattern worth watching — small specialized models displacing both heuristics and general LLMs.
results.verdict_reason: Interesting direction but an unreproduced single-source performance claim.
